title: Reinstatement Without Lapse on the RentGuard Renters Policy
content:
A RentGuard Renters Policy cancelled for nonpayment that is reinstated returns to force without a lapse, and the reinstatement is posted on the policy and its premium account in one recording.

## Rule

> Reinstatement is without a lapse: the term is unchanged, the reinstatement fee worked out under this rule is charged as one fee entry with fee code reinstatement fee, the cancellation credit is reversed by one additional premium entry with change reason reinstatement reversal for the same amount, referencing that credit and dated the reinstatement date, and the signed statement of no loss is marked completed.

> The reinstatement is not recorded until the premium account shows a payment received on or after the cancellation date that covers the cure amount.

Put the other way, while the premium account shows no payment received on or after the cancellation date that covers the cure amount, the reinstatement is not recorded.

## What a recorded reinstatement shows

| Item | Effect |
|---|---|
| Policy | back in force; the term is unchanged, so there is no lapse |
| Reinstatement fee | one fee entry with fee code reinstatement fee |
| Cancellation credit | reversed by one additional premium entry with change reason reinstatement reversal, for the same amount, referencing that credit and dated the reinstatement date |
| Statement of no loss | the signed statement is marked completed |

## Recording the reinstatement with `reinstate_lapsed_policy_e7e59896`

**Situation of use and capability.** The tool reinstates one cancelled RentGuard renters policy without a lapse. One call returns the policy to in force with its cancellation reason, cancellation date and scheduled action date cleared, charges one reinstatement fee entry of the amount given, records one additional premium entry with the reason reinstatement reversal for the reversal amount given that references the cancellation credit, both dated today, raises the premium balance by the two amounts, and marks the signed statement of no loss completed.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `renters_policy_id` — the reference number of the cancelled RentGuard renters policy record, as returned by the renters policy lookup for the customer (text id).
- `renters_request_id` — the reference number of the signed statement of no loss for this policy, as returned by the renters signature-request lookup (text id).
- `cancellation_credit_billing_id` — the reference number of the premium account entry that credited the cancellation, as returned by the renters premium account lookup (text id).
- `reversal_amount` — the amount of that cancellation credit, in USD with 2 decimal places, copied from the credit entry.
- `reinstatement_fee` — the reinstatement fee to charge, in USD with 2 decimal places, already rounded half-up to the cent; 0.00 records no fee entry.

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the policy reference now in force, the reinstatement fee entry reference (text id, or none when the fee is 0.00) and its amount, the reversal entry reference (text id) and its amount, all in USD with 2 decimal places, and the premium balance now standing. Receiving it means the policy is reinstated.

## Basis questions

**Does a reinstated policy start a new term?** No. Reinstatement is without a lapse and the term is unchanged.

**What amount does the reversal carry?** The same amount as the cancellation credit it references.

**What happens to the signed statement of no loss?** It is marked completed when the reinstatement is recorded.
